findings.description: The restructured `except ChevalError` branch in .claude/adapters/cheval.py records `str(_e)` into `models_failed[].message_redacted` and prints it to stderr via `_error_json` without passing it through `sanitize_provider_error_message`. The sibling preflight handler in the same diff imports and applies `_sanitize` to the exception text, and the following catch-all branch is documented as redacting known env-var secrets. ChevalError subclasses that wrap provider/CLI failures can carry upstream response bodies, URLs with query-string tokens, or header fragments. The modelinv.py docstring acknowledges `message_redacted` MAY hold raw upstream content and is redacted downstream, but the stderr JSON line has no such second pass. This path pre-dates the diff, but the diff rewrote the block and added a second unredacted emit site for the `opt_in_required` branch.
findings.failure_mode: A provider-originated ChevalError containing credential material (e.g., a bearer token echoed in an upstream 401 body or a signed URL) is written verbatim to stderr and into the operator-visible error JSON, where it is captured by CI logs, shell transcripts, or log shippers.
findings.suggested_fix: Route `str(_e)` through `sanitize_provider_error_message` (already imported locally as `_sanitize` in the preflight handler) before both the `models_failed` append and the `_error_json` print, matching the preflight and catch-all branches. Also guard `_fc` extraction with `isinstance(getattr(_e, 'context', None), dict)` so a non-dict context cannot raise inside the handler and escape the typed-exit path with a raw traceback.

findings.cross_file_justification: cheval.py (diff-touched) now rewrites `_chain` before `_modelinv_models_requested` is taken; modelinv.py (diff-touched) adds `models_not_planned` as an optional field that is omitted from the payload when empty. Audit consumers of the MODELINV event that key on `models_requested` alone lose visibility into dropped hops.
findings.description: The existing comment above the call states `models_requested` enumerates the entire resolved chain so audit consumers see the FULL intended walk shape. After this change, agy hops dropped by `_plan_around_agy` are removed from `models_requested` and surfaced only in the new optional `models_not_planned` field, which `emit_model_invoke_complete` omits entirely when falsy. The `_auth_type_resolved` value is also silently rewritten to the first kept hop's auth type. Existing downstream consumers, schema validators, or alerting that compare `models_requested` to the binding's declared chain will see a shorter chain with no indication a hop was removed unless they are updated to read the new field.
findings.failure_mode: An audit reviewer or compliance tool reconstructing which models were intended for a given invocation from `models_requested` sees a chain that does not match the configured binding, with the dropped hop recorded only in a field the consumer does not read. Policy drift (an agy hop silently added to a chain) is not detected by consumers that were written against the prior contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the full resolved chain in `models_requested` and mark planned-around hops via `models_not_planned` (so the invariant in the comment still holds), or update the comment and the MODELINV schema docs to state the new contract explicitly and emit `models_not_planned: []` unconditionally so consumers can distinguish 'nothing dropped' from 'field unsupported'. Record the original `_auth_type_resolved` alongside the rewritten one if both matter for audit.

findings.cross_file_justification: The gate is computed in .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py but enforced in .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py. complete(), validate_config() and health_check() call agy_opt_in_enabled() with no project_root, so _find_project_root()'s cwd walk from the reviewed tree decides whether agy is dispatched.
findings.description: The opt-in that authorizes the agy route (prompt on argv readable by all local users, `agy --sandbox --dangerously-skip-permissions` on untrusted review content) is read from `.loa.config.yaml` discovered by walking up from cheval's cwd. The adapter's own module docstring identifies that cwd as the reviewed tree whose settings 'would shape its own reviewer', which is why agy's cwd was moved to a private workspace. The gate nonetheless anchors its trust in a file inside that same tree. When the review pipeline runs on a checkout of a PR head (CI-style flows), the PR author controls that file and can set `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true`, defeating the 'operator decision' guarantee the docstrings make ('never talked into the agy voice by ambient env'; 'exposed only by an operator's deliberate choice'). On a host with agy OAuth-authed this enables the exposed-argv dispatch and the agentic run on the PR's content; on a host without agy it turns a cleanly not-planned voice into a hard ConfigError, degrading the verdict.
findings.failure_mode: A PR adds or edits `.loa.config.yaml` with `agy_opt_in: true`. The reviewing cheval process, running with cwd in the PR checkout, reads it as opted in, passes the adapter check, and spawns agy with the PR-controlled prompt on argv under --dangerously-skip-permissions, or fails the Google voice with INVALID_CONFIG where agy is absent. Exploitability depends on deployment: local reviews against a trusted main checkout are not affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Source the opt-in from an operator-controlled location outside the reviewed tree (a user-level or host-level config, or an explicit trusted root passed by cheval rather than the cwd walk), or at minimum read it from the base ref's `.loa.config.yaml` rather than the PR head and refuse when the diff under review touches that file. Pass the resolved trusted root explicitly into the adapter instead of relying on the ambient cwd.

findings.description: The gate documents itself as 'no discovery, workspace, WARN or spawn while it is off' and 'A PATH lookup only: nothing is spawned', but the no-PyYAML fallback spawns `yq` resolved from PATH up to three times on every evaluation. Because agy_opt_in_enabled() is uncached and called from complete(), validate_config(), health_check() and warn_agy_available_once(), a PATH-resolved external binary runs on every hop and every health probe, including when the route is off. A planted `yq` earlier on PATH can return `true` / `!!bool` and flip the gate open; the gate otherwise fails closed only on non-zero exit or exception, not on a tampered answer.
findings.failure_mode: On a host without PyYAML, each gate evaluation executes whatever `yq` PATH resolves to with the config path as an argument. A malicious or buggy `yq` can report the key as a `!!bool true` and enable the route; a slow one adds up to 15 seconds of latency per hop before the 5-second timeouts fail closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer requiring PyYAML (it is already the primary path) or resolve `yq` via an absolute, operator-pinned path. Evaluate the gate once per process (or memoize per config path and mtime) so the file is read and any subprocess runs at most once rather than per hop. Update the docstrings to state that the fallback does spawn.

findings.description: The PyYAML path derives `kind` with `(node.tag or '').rsplit(':', 1)[-1]`, so any tag whose last colon-separated segment is `bool` is accepted. A scalar written `agy_opt_in: !<x:bool> true` yields kind == 'bool' and text == 'true' and opts in, while the yq fallback and the bash reader (which keep the full tag) read the same node as off. This breaks the documented 'ONE strict rule with the bash reader' invariant, and the divergence is in the permissive direction for the Python reader that actually performs the dispatch.
findings.failure_mode: The Python adapter dispatches agy (argv prompt exposure) for a config the bash planner and the yq fallback treat as not opted in, so the two readers disagree about whether the route is live.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the full tag exactly: `node.tag == 'tag:yaml.org,2002:bool'`, and in the yq fallback require `tag == '!!bool'` exactly rather than stripping a `!!` prefix.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new tests pin that loa_cheval.config.loader.agy_opt_in_enabled() resolves the project root by walking up from the process cwd (test_the_project_root_defaults_to_the_cwd_walk) and that AgyHeadlessAdapter calls it with no explicit root, re-reading .loa.config.yaml on every dispatch (test_the_adapter_reads_the_real_project_config). test_no_environment_override and test_g9_system_defaults_alone_never_opt_in confirm the repo-tree file is the sole input to the gate.
findings.description: The opt-in gate exists (per the refusal text) to protect the operator from the prompt riding argv, readable by other local users, and from agy running with --dangerously-skip-permissions. Its only input is a file inside the project tree. Anyone who controls repo contents (a PR branch the operator checks out to review, a vendored submodule, a workspace under /run/user/1000/loa-claude-ws) can ship .claude/ plus .loa.config.yaml with agy_opt_in: true and the route silently activates with no operator action. There is no operator-owned source (home-dir config, per-project trust record) that must also agree, and no log of which file flipped the gate.
findings.failure_mode: Operator runs a review from inside an untrusted checkout. The checkout's config opts in. The full prompt, including the reviewed diff, is placed on the agy argv and agy is launched with permission checks skipped, without the operator ever having set the key.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the opt-in from an operator-owned location (e.g. ~/.loa/config.yaml or a trust record outside the tree) in addition to, or instead of, the repo file. At minimum, log the absolute path of the file that enabled the route on the first dispatch, and add a test asserting a repo-supplied true without operator trust reads off.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test sets loader._HAS_YAML = False and relies on shutil.which('yq'), showing that loa_cheval.config.loader evaluates the security gate by spawning whatever yq is first on PATH when PyYAML is absent.
findings.description: A security-relevant decision is delegated to an unpinned third-party binary found on PATH. python-yq (the jq wrapper) and go-yq disagree on tag/!!bool expressions, so the strict rule the test asserts only holds for one implementation. The test skips when yq is missing, so CI most likely never exercises this fallback at all. A yq planted earlier on PATH that prints true opens the gate; fail-closed on error does not cover a successful wrong answer.
findings.failure_mode: Hosts without PyYAML get a gate whose strictness is untested in CI and depends on which yq flavor happens to be installed or planted.
findings.suggested_fix: When PyYAML is unavailable, read the key as off and emit the one-time warning rather than consulting yq. If the fallback must stay, verify yq --version identifies go-yq before trusting its output, and make the test fail rather than skip in CI (or vendor a stub) so the fallback is actually covered.

findings.description: Gate coverage asserts only complete(), health_check() and validate_config() refuse when off. TestCommandConstruction._cmd shows _build_command is callable without passing the gate, and no test enumerates the adapter's other spawn-capable entrypoints (streaming, async, or any future method). The new autouse fixture forces the gate open for every test in test_agy_headless_adapter.py, so the legacy suite can no longer catch a path that forgets the gate.
findings.failure_mode: A later entrypoint spawns agy without consulting agy_opt_in_enabled and the whole suite stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Route every spawn through a single chokepoint that performs the gate check and test that chokepoint directly; or add a test that introspects the adapter's public spawn-capable methods and asserts each raises AgyOptInRequiredError when the gate is off.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff-touched config example documents, and the diff-touched test_headless_argv_nul_robustness.py docstring and _ARGV_ADAPTERS table confirm, that gemini-headless (agy) is the only adapter that still passes the UNTRUSTED prompt on argv via `-p <prompt>`. The sink lives in agy_headless_adapter.py (not in the diff); the diff adds the operator-facing switch that enables that path and the autouse fixtures that force it on in two test modules.
findings.description: When hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in is set true, the entire review prompt (persona text plus the redacted diff under review) is placed on the agy child process's command line. On Linux, /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable by default, so any other local account, any container sharing the PID namespace, and any process-monitoring agent can read the full prompt for as long as the agy call runs. argv is also captured in auditd execve records, process accounting, and crash reports. The new opt-in default and its WARN text reduce exposure but do not remove it; redaction is the only content control, and the diff's own test suite pins agy as the sole argv-prompt adapter. Grok already uses --prompt-file and claude/codex/cursor use stdin, so a non-argv transport is the established pattern in this codebase.
findings.failure_mode: An operator enables agy_opt_in on a shared CI runner or multi-user developer host. A lower-privileged local user (or a compromised sidecar process) polls `ps -o args` or reads /proc/*/cmdline during a review and recovers proprietary source plus any credentials that survived redaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the prompt off argv in agy_headless_adapter: if agy accepts a prompt on stdin or from a file, pass it via `input=` or a 0600 temp file (mirror the grok --prompt-file pattern). If agy cannot, keep the default off and have agy_opt_in_enabled additionally refuse or WARN unless /proc is mounted with hidepid>=1. Add a test asserting the prompt bytes never appear in the spawned argv once a non-argv path exists, and keep the no-environment-override property documented in the config example.

findings.cross_file_justification: The guard lives in .claude/scripts/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh (new in diff); the fail-open manifests in the diff-touched hard-sourcing callers flatline-orchestrator.sh (get_model_tertiary, agy_gate_warn_once in main), run-preflight.sh (P3 loop) and loa-status.sh (_provider_hop, _AGY_OPT_IN_NOTE).
findings.description: The include guard reads `${_LOA_AGY_GATE_LIB_LOADED:-}`, which resolves from the process environment as well as the current shell. An exported `_LOA_AGY_GATE_LIB_LOADED=1` (or a parent running under `set -a`) makes `source lib/agy-gate-lib.sh` return before any function or constant is defined. flatline-orchestrator.sh, run-preflight.sh and loa-status.sh hard-source the lib and never check `declare -F routes_to_agy`. Their predicates then run as `routes_to_agy: command not found` (exit 127, i.e. false): `get_model_tertiary` keeps an agy-routed tertiary and `get_tertiary_status` reports `active`; preflight P3 counts a `gemini-headless` voice as usable whenever `agy` is on PATH; loa-status reports `cli_hop: agy` with no `cli_hop_note`. `_LOA_AGY_GATE_WARNED` is likewise seeded from env, so the G12/G18 warning can be pre-suppressed. Under `set -e`/`set -u` the same env instead aborts the orchestrator at the top-level `agy_gate_warn_once` call or loa-status at `_AGY_OPT_IN_NOTE="$AGY_OPT_IN_NOTE"`. This contradicts the header's stated invariant that no environment value can talk a planner into the route. adversarial-review.sh is not affected because `_adv_agy_lib` checks `declare -F` and falls back to name-based fail-closed filtering.
findings.failure_mode: Ambient environment silently removes the planner-level agy opt-in gate: an agy-routed tertiary or voice is planned and reported as active/usable while hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in is absent or false, leaving cheval's Python gate as the only control; alternatively the orchestrator or status script crashes on load.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the guard shell-only, e.g. `declare -F agy_opted_in >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0` instead of an env-readable variable, and set `_LOA_AGY_GATE_WARNED=''` unconditionally. In every hard-sourcing caller, verify `declare -F routes_to_agy agy_opted_in agy_headless_mode >/dev/null` after sourcing and either exit or fall back to the same name-based fail-closed behaviour adversarial-review.sh uses.

findings.description: `_anthropic_ceiling_json` in loa-status.sh reads `.aliases.opus` from the model catalog and splices it unquoted into yq expressions of the form `.providers.anthropic.models."$model".…`; the diff adds a fourth such read (`transport=`). A value containing a double quote breaks out of the string literal and runs arbitrary yq; mikefarah yq exposes `load()`/`load_str()`, which read any readable file into the result that then lands in the status JSON. run-preflight.sh guards the identical sink in `provider_of` with `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$` and the comment 'config text is operator-owned but is still input'; loa-status applies no check. The catalog is repo-owned, so exploitation requires a catalog edit or the env-selected catalog path from the new `_providers_model_config` seam (see AGY-003).
findings.failure_mode: A crafted `aliases.opus` value in the catalog (or an env-redirected catalog) injects into the yq expression and can pull arbitrary local file contents into loa-status output.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `$model` with the same character-class regex used by run-preflight.sh `provider_of` before interpolation, or pass it out-of-band (`M="$model" yq eval '.providers.anthropic.models[strenv(M)].…'`).

findings.description: `_providers_config_file` and `_providers_model_config` in loa-status.sh switch to caller-supplied paths (`LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE`, `LOA_STATUS_MODEL_CONFIG`) whenever `BATS_TEST_FILENAME` or `BATS_VERSION` is non-empty. Nothing verifies the process is actually under bats, so any invoker can export `BATS_VERSION=x LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE=/tmp/x.yaml` and have `/loa-status`, including the machine JSON that 'callers merge', report the agy route as opted in, `cli_hop: agy`, and no `cli_hop_note`, while the real `.loa.config.yaml` says off. The same seam selects the catalog read by the yq interpolation in AGY-002. Display-only, but this is the surface operators use to confirm the gate is in place.
findings.failure_mode: Environment alone changes which config the Providers block reports on, so loa-status can be made to show the agy route enabled or disabled regardless of the real configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate test seams on an explicit, non-inheritable switch (e.g. honour the override only when `LOA_TEST_SEAMS=1` is set by the test harness) or inject fixtures through a `--config <path>` argument rather than env vars named after bats.

findings.description: `_adv_agy_lib` in adversarial-review.sh lazily sources `${PROJECT_ROOT:-}/.claude/scripts/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh`, whereas the top-of-file source of the same lib and every other lib in the script use `$SCRIPT_DIR`. If `PROJECT_ROOT` is, or later becomes, env-overridable, the file executed with the reviewer's credentials and API keys is chosen by the caller. The function is also reached from inside `$(…)` filter calls where a sourcing error is swallowed by `2>/dev/null`. The derivation of PROJECT_ROOT in this file could not be verified from the diff.
findings.failure_mode: A caller-controlled PROJECT_ROOT leads to sourcing arbitrary shell code into the adversarial-review process.
findings.suggested_fix: Source from the already-computed `$_AGY_GATE_LIB_PATH` (`$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh`) in the lazy path as well, keeping the `declare -F` verification.

findings.cross_file_justification: routes_to_agy in lib/agy-gate-lib.sh matches literal id forms only; flatline-orchestrator.sh (_tertiary_routes_to_agy) and run-preflight.sh (P3 loop) pass the raw configured id, while adversarial-review.sh (_adv_agy_filter_chain) also tests the _adv_hop_canon result, so the three diff-touched planners disagree on what is gated.
findings.description: `routes_to_agy` recognises only `gemini-headless`, `*:gemini-headless`, `gemini-headless:*`, and `gemini*` under cli-only, case-sensitively. flatline-orchestrator's `_tertiary_routes_to_agy` and run-preflight P3 pass the raw configured id with no catalog alias resolution; adversarial-review tests both the raw hop and its canonical id. A tertiary configured via a catalog alias that resolves to a gemini-headless target, or written as `google:gemini-headless:<m>` or in mixed case, is therefore planned by flatline (status `active`), counted usable by preflight, and dropped by the companion-chain planner. The name-based fallback in `_adv_agy_filter_chain` also omits the `*:gemini-headless:*` form. Enforcement then rests entirely on cheval's Python twin, and the status/metadata surfaces misreport why a voice did or did not run.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent gating across planners: an alias- or prefix-spelled agy hop is planned and reported active by flatline and preflight while the opt-in is off, and the run degrades at dispatch instead of being reported as disabled_by_opt_in.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve aliases through the shared catalog before calling routes_to_agy (flatline already sources generated-model-maps.sh / resolve_provider_id; preflight has provider_of's alias lookup), lower-case the id, and add the `*:gemini-headless:*` pattern to both routes_to_agy and the adversarial-review name fallback.

findings.description: run-preflight.sh sources lib/agy-gate-lib.sh with no failure guard. The script runs under `set -uo pipefail` without `-e`, so a missing or unreadable lib prints one error and execution continues. Every gate call then hits an undefined function: `agy_headless_mode` yields an empty p3_mode, `agy_opted_in` returns 127 so p3_agy_on stays 0, and `routes_to_agy` returns 127, which bash treats as false. The opt-in test `(( ! p3_agy_on )) && routes_to_agy ...` therefore never gates anything and the K3 line `routes_to_agy ... && cli=agy` never fires. A `gemini-headless` voice with an `agy` binary on PATH is reported usable and P3 can PASS. This is the opposite of the fail-closed behaviour the same change adds to adversarial-review.sh and pins with CMP-287 (lib missing → hop dropped with reason opt_in_required). The two readers disagree exactly when the shared predicate is absent, which is the condition the conformance suite says must never happen.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight reports a stage as having a usable voice while the dissent planner, failing closed, drops that voice at run time. An operator launching an unattended run on the strength of P3 PASS gets a stage with no voice or a DEGRADED verdict, including for security_audit. Impact is advisory and availability-shaped, not a privilege boundary: preflight itself never dispatches agy or reads a credential value.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the source: `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh" || { echo "run-preflight: agy-gate-lib.sh not loaded" >&2; exit 2; }`. Alternatively define fail-closed stubs before sourcing (`agy_opted_in() { return 1; }` and a `routes_to_agy` that returns 0 for any `gemini*` / `*gemini-headless*` id) so a missing lib yields opt_in_required rather than usable. Add a run-preflight.bats case mirroring CMP-287 that unsets the lib functions and asserts P3 reports the hop as not planned.

findings.description: Model ids read from .loa.config.yaml are expanded unquoted in `for m in $models $chain`, so they undergo word splitting and pathname expansion. A token such as `*` or `gemini-?` enumerates files in the current directory as voices. Each resulting name is passed to `provider_of` (shape-checked before yq, safe), `cli_for` (closed case, safe), the new `routes_to_agy` call in the shared lib (no shape check applied in this file), and is concatenated raw into p3_optin / usable_names / missing, which reach the terminal via `echo` and the JSON detail field. The loop line itself is unchanged context, but the diff adds three new consumers of `$m` inside it without adding validation. Config is operator-owned, so no privilege boundary is crossed; this is hardening only.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed or hostile config entry inflates the voice list with filenames, produces misleading P3 counts (n_voices, n_gated), and can inject arbitrary bytes including ANSI escape sequences into the human-readable preflight output. No command execution results because every sink is a string compare, `command -v` on a fixed binary name, or text output.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable globbing for the loop (`set -f` before, `set +f` after) or read the values with `mapfile -t` into arrays and iterate quoted. Apply the same `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$` shape check already used in provider_of at the top of the loop and record ids that fail it as a WARN rather than feeding them to routes_to_agy and the detail string.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/run-preflight.bats:@test "PF-AGY-4 (review r251-1 G12): a string agy_opt_in reads off with one WARN naming the key and the type; --json stays quiet on stderr"
findings.trigger_anchor: tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats:@test "FTA-1 an agy tertiary with the opt-in absent, false or a string is not planned; the reason names the key"
findings.description: The hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in gate decides whether review content is dispatched to the external Antigravity (agy) route. The diff shows it is parsed independently by three consumers: flatline-orchestrator.sh (FTA-1..5, bash), the /loa status script (LSP-AGY), and run-preflight (PF-AGY-4, whose WARN text reports a Python type name '(str)', implying PyYAML). The new tests only exercise the values true, false, absent, and the quoted string "true". None exercise YAML 1.1 truthy literals (yes, on, True, 1) or duplicate hounfour keys (PF-AGY and PF-AGY-4 append a hounfour: block to an existing file). PyYAML (YAML 1.1) decodes yes/on as booleans; yq v4 (YAML 1.2) decodes them as strings. A parser divergence between consumers is exactly the failure this gate exists to prevent, and the test suite would not detect it.
findings.failure_mode: An operator writes agy_opt_in: yes. Preflight and status report 'agy: opt-in (disabled)' while the orchestrator's parser treats the value as boolean true and sends review documents through the agy route the operator believes is off. The reverse divergence makes preflight PASS a voice the orchestrator never plans, silently degrading to 2-model mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one table-driven case list (yes, on, True, 1, "true", true, false, absent, duplicate key) and run it in all three test files, asserting identical verdicts from get_tertiary_status, the status JSON cli_hop_note, and the preflight P3 line. Preferably route all three consumers through a single shared boolean-parsing helper so the tests pin one implementation.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats:@test "FTA-4 a non-agy tertiary and an unset tertiary are unchanged by the gate"
findings.trigger_anchor: tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats:@test "FTA-4 a non-agy tertiary and an unset tertiary are unchanged by the gate"
findings.description: FTA-4 verifies the gate defaults off when the opt-in key or the tertiary model is absent, but no test covers an unreadable CONFIG_FILE, malformed YAML, or the YAML tool missing from PATH. get_tertiary_status and tertiary_opt_in_skip_reason are only observed on well-formed input, so fail-closed behaviour on the error path is unverified for a gate that controls an external dispatch.
findings.failure_mode: A yq failure or a syntax error in .loa.config.yaml yields an empty status string; downstream Phase 1 code compares against 'disabled_by_opt_in', finds no match, and proceeds to dispatch or logs a 'Voice dropped' DEGRADED path instead of the opt-in skip.
findings.suggested_fix: Add FTA cases for a missing config file, a malformed YAML body, and yq removed from PATH. Assert get_model_tertiary returns empty, get_tertiary_status returns a disabled value, and run_phase1 makes no tertiary call.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new test file pins the contract of isAgyRouted in resources/config.ts: a google model is treated as agy-routed only under mode cli-only (or the gemini-headless id). The dispatch side is ChevalDelegateAdapter, whose headless mode comes from LOA_HEADLESS_MODE or hounfour.headless.mode. If cheval's prefer-cli semantics are 'try the CLI hop first, fall back to HTTP' (which the name implies), a google voice under prefer-cli passes the gate as 'planned' and is then handed to the agy CLI hop with the opt-in off.
findings.description: The opt-in gate only classifies a google voice as agy-routed under mode cli-only. Under prefer-cli the same voice is planned, counted, and dispatched, yet cheval in prefer-cli mode would most plausibly try the gemini CLI (Antigravity) hop before HTTP. The test 'LOA_HEADLESS_MODE wins for the mode ... nothing in the environment opts in' also shows the mode is environment-selectable, so setting LOA_HEADLESS_MODE=prefer-cli in the runner environment is enough to steer google voices toward the agy hop without hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in being true. I could not read config.ts or cheval to confirm the fallback order, so this is flagged as a design gap the tests lock in rather than a verified exploit.
findings.failure_mode: PR diff content and review prompts are sent through the Antigravity CLI route for a repository whose operator never opted in, contradicting FR-1 ('the agy route is opt-in, default false'). The gate reports the voice as planned and the summary shows a full cohort, so nothing in the logs says the hop was taken.
findings.suggested_fix: Either treat prefer-cli as agy-routed for google models in isAgyRouted (gate on 'may hit the CLI' rather than 'must hit the CLI'), or have the pipeline pass an explicit no-CLI/HTTP-only flag to the cheval adapter for google voices when the opt-in is off. Add a test asserting isAgyRouted("google", <non-headless id>, "prefer-cli") is true, or a dispatch-level test that the adapter receives an API-only directive.

findings.trigger_anchor: .claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/__tests__/multi-model-agy-opt-in.test.ts: describe("validateApiKeys takes the gate explicitly (r251-1 G15)")
findings.description: The gate's source file is resolved relative to the process cwd when no repo root is given, and otherwise from config.repoRoot. A security-relevant policy flag (whether PR content may leave via the Antigravity hop) therefore depends on where the process is launched and on whose .loa.config.yaml sits at repoRoot. The pipeline tests pass a temp dir as repoRoot; if repoRoot can ever be a checkout of the repository under review, the PR author controls the opt-in. I could not verify how repoRoot is populated in main.ts.
findings.failure_mode: Launching the reviewer from a directory containing an attacker- or stale-authored .loa.config.yaml with agy_opt_in: true silently enables the agy route. Fail-closed on read errors mitigates malformed files but not a well-formed hostile one.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the Loa config from the tool's own installation or an explicit absolute path rather than cwd, and document (or assert in a test) that repoRoot is never the reviewed repository's PR head checkout. Consider logging the resolved config path at startup via agyGateStartupLines.

findings.anchor: assert.ok(!result.reviewVerdict.mergeBlocked, "a not-planned voice never blocks the merge as a missing one would");
findings.trigger_anchor: .claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/__tests__/multi-model-agy-opt-in.test.ts: describe("executeMultiModelReview with the agy opt-in off")
findings.description: The tests pin that a configured reviewer voice removed by the gate is excluded from voices_planned, so a three-voice config posts '✓ APPROVED — 2/2 voices' with merge not blocked, and under api_key_mode strict the pipeline only WARNs instead of failing. The posted summary is not asserted to mention the not-planned voice. Readers of the PR comment see a full cohort even though the configured review coverage was silently reduced, and strict mode no longer means 'every configured voice ran or the review fails'.
findings.failure_mode: Review coverage degrades without a visible signal on the PR itself; an operator relying on strict mode to guarantee all configured reviewers ran gets a passing verdict with a reviewer missing.
findings.suggested_fix: In strict mode, treat a gated-off configured voice the same as a missing key (throw) or require an explicit acknowledgement setting. In graceful mode, include the not-planned voices in the posted Verdict Quality summary (e.g. '2/2 planned, 1 not planned: google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview (opt-in required)') and add a test asserting it.

findings.trigger_anchor: const gated = gate.readError !== undefined ? model.provider === "google" : isAgyRouted(model.provider, model.model_id, gate.mode);
findings.cross_file_justification: config.ts (diff-touched) marks every google voice notPlanned whenever readAgyGate reports readError; multi-model-pipeline.ts (diff-touched) then subtracts notPlanned from the required participant count for the merge gate and skips the strict-mode throw for those voices.
findings.description: The agy gate is documented as fail-closed, but its failure mode fails OPEN for the two controls that matter. When `yq` is absent, times out, or `.loa.config.yaml` is malformed, `validateApiKeys` moves every google voice to `notPlanned`. In `executeMultiModelReview` that has two effects: (1) `api_key_mode: "strict"` no longer throws for those voices — it only logs a warn — so a strict-mode operator gets a review with fewer voices than configured; (2) the merge-block invariant (`modelResults.length !== models.length - notPlanned.length`) is satisfied with the reduced set, so a verdict from the remaining voices can clear `mergeBlocked`. A review host missing `yq`, or a repo whose `.loa.config.yaml` is unreadable, therefore lowers the reviewer quorum rather than blocking merge. The pre-change comment states the invariant explicitly: 'Incomplete or degraded participation can never clear a merge.'
findings.failure_mode: A configured 3-voice strict review (anthropic, openai, google) runs on a host without `yq` or with a corrupt `.loa.config.yaml`. The google voice is silently dropped at warn level, strict mode does not fail, and the two remaining voices can produce an APPROVED band that clears `mergeBlocked`. If `repoRoot` ever points at a PR-head checkout, the PR author can trigger this by corrupting `.loa.config.yaml`.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat `gate.readError` as a hard failure for strict mode (throw, as missing keys do) and keep `mergeBlocked = true` whenever `keyStatus.notPlanned` is non-empty due to a read error. Only subtract voices from the required count when the opt-in was read successfully and is explicitly false. Consider also pinning the merge gate to `multiConfig.models.length` and recording not-planned voices as a separate, non-clearing degradation.

findings.description: The agy opt-in that decides whether google voices are dispatched through the Antigravity CLI (spending operator-side CLI auth/quota) or dropped from the review is read from `.loa.config.yaml` under `config.repoRoot`, falling back to the current working directory. This is repository- and cwd-controlled data governing a routing decision, not operator-controlled configuration (env/CLI). The code correctly refuses to let the environment opt IN, but it lets a repo file do so. Whether this is exploitable depends on whether `repoRoot` can ever be a checkout of untrusted PR content; from the diff alone that cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_mode: If the reviewer runs against a checkout containing the PR under review, the PR author can flip `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` to route google voices through the operator's agy CLI session, or set it false / corrupt the file to remove the google reviewer from quorum (see SEC-1).
findings.suggested_fix: Document and enforce that `repoRoot` is the operator's trusted checkout, or read the opt-in from an operator-owned location (e.g. `~/.loa/config.yaml` or an explicit CLI flag) with the repo file as a lower-priority source that can only turn the route OFF.

findings.trigger_anchor: ? `not planned: ${notPlannedList} (the agy gate failed closed: Loa config unreadable — ${agyGate.readError}; hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in)`
findings.cross_file_justification: config.ts captures raw yq stderr / Node error text into `readError`; multi-model-pipeline.ts interpolates it into a thrown Error message and warn logs; main.ts prints it via agyGateStartupLines.
findings.description: `readError` carries the first 300 chars of raw `yq` stderr or the Node spawn error (`spawnSync yq ENOENT`, absolute path of `.loa.config.yaml`, yq parse diagnostics). It is interpolated into the `No models available` Error thrown from `executeMultiModelReview`. If that error text is ever surfaced in a PR comment or run summary rather than only in operator logs, it leaks local filesystem paths and tool inventory of the review host.
findings.failure_mode: An unreadable config causes the pipeline to throw with a message containing the host's absolute config path and yq's raw diagnostic; any caller that posts or persists the error message externally exposes host details.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a short, fixed reason code in `readError` for user-facing strings (e.g. `yq-missing`, `yaml-parse-error`) and log the raw stderr separately at debug level; avoid interpolating raw subprocess stderr into thrown Error messages.

findings.anchor: '{"opt": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | (tag == "!!bool" and . == true)), "canon": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | (tag == "!!bool" and (. == true or . == false))), "tag": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | tag), "mode": (.hounfour.headless.mode // "")}',
findings.description: The `canon` check is dead: once yq has tagged a scalar `!!bool`, `. == true or . == false` is always true, so the 'boolean spelled other than true/false' warning can never fire. Meanwhile yq v4 accepts `True`, `TRUE`, `False` as `!!bool`, so those spellings DO opt in here. The comment claims the bash reader (`lib/agy-gate-lib.sh`) and the Python reader apply the same strict rule; a bash reader doing a literal `== true` match would disagree, producing a gate that plans a google voice in TypeScript which cheval then refuses (or vice versa). The gate is a security-relevant routing decision and the three readers should agree on exactly which inputs opt in.
findings.failure_mode: `agy_opt_in: True` opts in via this reader but may not via the bash gate, so BB dispatches a google voice that cheval rejects (or the reverse), yielding inconsistent planned/not-planned accounting across the pipeline and the quorum math in SEC-1.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the raw scalar text rather than the normalized value, e.g. add `"raw": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | tostring)` and require `raw == "true"` in TypeScript; add a parity test that feeds `True`, `yes`, `"true"`, and `true` to all three readers and asserts identical results. Remove the dead `canon` branch.

findings.description: The new module-level builder emits the prompt as a bare argv element immediately after `-p`, and appends `effort` and `cli_model` with no allowlist validation. The repository's own comments state the prompt is untrusted. Option parsers treat a value that begins with `-` as a new flag rather than as the argument to `-p`, so attacker-influenced leading prompt text (or a malformed `cli_model` / `effort` from config) becomes an injected CLI option in the `claude` invocation. The shape is pre-existing, but the refactor made it a shared public function consumed by callers outside the adapter (tools/ceiling-probe-live.py), widening the surface without adding validation.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt or config value starting with `--` is consumed by the claude CLI as an option. Depending on the flag, this can alter permission mode, tool enablement, output format, or cause the real prompt to be dropped and read from stdin, undermining the "pure inference, all tools disabled" guarantee the argv is meant to enforce.
findings.suggested_fix: Always deliver the prompt on stdin (the existing prompt=None path) so no untrusted text appears in argv. Validate `effort` against EFFORT_LEVELS and `cli_model` against a strict identifier regex (e.g. ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$ and not starting with `-`) inside build_headless_argv, raising ConfigError on mismatch. Add a unit test asserting a `-`-prefixed prompt/model never reaches argv.

findings.anchor: if is_context_limit_message(full_diag) and not any(w in diag_lower for w in _throttle_words):
findings.description: The new ProviderContextLimitError branch decides a failed `claude -p` run was a provider size rejection by pattern-matching free text in `full_diag`. If that aggregate includes stdout (the model's own output) or echoed prompt fragments, prompt-injected content such as "Prompt is too long ... (limit 1000000)" is classified as the provider's verdict. Per the inline comment, that class of error is deliberately "not walked" and "never a breaker count".
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted content can steer failure classification: fallback-voice routing is suppressed and circuit-breaker accounting is bypassed for the affected provider, pinning repeated failures to one voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the context-limit check only against stderr or the CLI's structured JSON error fields (is_error / subtype / message), not the combined diagnostic string. Anchor is_context_limit_message to the CLI's exact message format and require the parsed numbers to be present before raising ProviderContextLimitError.

findings.anchor: f"claude CLI refused the prompt as too large: {full_diag[:500]}"
findings.description: Up to 500 characters of raw CLI stderr/stdout are embedded in the exception message, which propagates into MODELINV envelopes, logs, and user-facing error output. CLI diagnostics can carry local filesystem paths, session or account identifiers, and echoed prompt content.
findings.failure_mode: Operator paths, account hints, or confidential prompt fragments leak into persisted envelopes and shared logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Log the raw diagnostic at debug level only. Put just the parsed values (input_tokens, limit, max_tokens) and a fixed message in the exception string.

findings.description: ClaudeHeadlessAdapter.wire_effort and CodexHeadlessAdapter.wire_effort invoke instance resolvers on `cls.__new__(cls)` (no __init__, so self.config and self.provider are absent) with a SimpleNamespace standing in for model_config. The `effort_effective` audit record is only faithful while `_resolve_effort` / `_resolve_reasoning_effort` remain pure functions of (request.effort, extra). Any future reference to instance state or other model_config attributes will either raise AttributeError in the envelope path or silently make the recorded effort diverge from the argv it is meant to certify.
findings.failure_mode: Integrity of the effort_effective record degrades silently, or envelope construction crashes, without any test catching the drift between record and dispatched argv.
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor the resolvers into static/class methods that take (effort, extra) explicitly and have both complete() and wire_effort call that single pure function. Extend tests/test_effort_wire_conformance.py to assert wire_effort equals the `--effort` / `model_reasoning_effort` value produced by the real argv builder.

findings.description: GrokHeadlessAdapter.wire_effort constructs an uninitialized adapter with cls.__new__(cls), skipping __init__ (no config, logger, or circuit-breaker state), builds a synthetic CompletionRequest(messages=[]) and calls _resolve_reasoning_effort on that bare object. This is the value cheval records as effort_effective in the MODELINV audit envelope for xai routes. Any instance-attribute access inside _resolve_reasoning_effort, including a warning path that formats self.config or self.name, raises AttributeError at audit time. Because the value is derived by a side path rather than read back from the argv that _build_command actually emits, the audit field can silently diverge from the real --reasoning-effort token. The method also accepts an effort argument that its own docstring says is ignored, and it assumes CompletionRequest is a runtime import in this module. The new test module adds no test for wire_effort; _effort_on_wire coverage stops at anthropic and openai.
findings.failure_mode: On a grok-headless invocation, computing effort_effective either throws (aborting or failing the invoke depending on where _effort_on_wire is called relative to dispatch) or records a value that does not match the subprocess argv. The audit trail for model invocations becomes unreliable on exactly the provider whose effort handling differs from the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the reasoning-effort resolver a pure staticmethod that takes only the extra mapping and call it from both _build_command and wire_effort, or have wire_effort invoke the real argv builder and read the --reasoning-effort value back. Remove the ignored effort parameter or document it explicitly. Wrap the call site in cheval so an exception degrades to effort_effective=None with a WARN rather than failing the invoke. Add a unit test for wire_effort and an xai case to test_effort_on_wire_follows_the_adapter_mapping.

findings.description: The dry-run subprocess helper copies the full parent environment and removes only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK and CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN. Every other provider credential cheval can read (OpenAI, xAI, Google/Gemini, OpenRouter, and any future one) still reaches a child process that runs the complete cheval.py entrypoint. Safety depends solely on --dry-run never dispatching.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in dry-run gating, or a test edit that drops the --dry-run flag, makes the suite perform live, billed API calls with the developer's or CI runner's real credentials. Captured stdout/stderr then appears in assertion messages and CI logs, which may include provider error bodies.
findings.suggested_fix: Construct the child environment from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, PYTHONPATH, LANG/LC_*, TMPDIR) rather than a deny-list, and inject placeholder values for any variable cheval needs to resolve a provider in dry-run mode.

findings.description: The in-process invoke helper patches loa_cheval.audit.modelinv.redact_payload_strings to the identity function and assert_no_secret_shapes_remain to a no-op before capturing the MODELINV payload. All assertions on effort, effort_source and effort_effective therefore run against the pre-redaction payload. The new envelope fields are never shown to survive the redaction gate, and the secret-shape assertion that normally guards the audit sink is silenced for every test in this module.
findings.failure_mode: A redaction change that strips or rewrites the new fields, or a regression that lets a secret-shaped string into the envelope alongside them, passes this suite unnoticed. The tests give false assurance about what actually lands in the audit log.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep redaction and the secret-shape assertion active (they should be no-ops for these payloads) and stub only audit_emit. If the identity patch exists to dodge a specific redaction false positive, scope it to that single test and add an explicit assertion that the real redactor preserves effort_source and effort_effective.

findings.cross_file_justification: effective_input_ceiling is consumed by cheval's pre-flight gate (exit 7 ContextTooLarge) and routing/ceiling.input_bound, as documented in .claude/data/schemas/model-config-v3.schema.json (effective_input_ceiling and probed_ceiling descriptions). The catalog entry edited in this diff is the trigger; the gate and the fallback chain that act on it live in cheval.py and the routing layer, which are not in the diff.
findings.description: The anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 entry (the HTTP-API route; it carries beta_headers and falls back to anthropic:claude-headless) has both probed_ceiling and effective_input_ceiling raised from 180000 to 936000, a 5.2x loosening of the pre-flight input gate. The evidence basis recorded alongside it is weak for this route: probe_outcome is partial, method is probed_headless, transport is claude-headless, and cli_model is the Bedrock inference profile global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5. The reprobe_trigger text itself states the API transport was never measured. The same entry keeps beta_headers: [] (no 1M-context beta flag) and account_limits tier unverified / itpm null. Setting source: operator_set with a calibrated_at timestamp flips the entry from uncalibrated (where probed_ceiling 180000 governed) to calibrated, so 936000 now governs every request on the direct API route.
findings.failure_mode: Two effects. (1) Cost blast radius: any caller, including automated review/audit loops whose context size is influenced by untrusted input such as a large PR diff, can now send ~936k input tokens per call before any gate fires (roughly $3.74 vs $0.72 of input at the listed $4/MTok), a 5x amplifier on per-invocation spend with no API-side verification that the account tier even accepts it. (2) Routing bypass: if the direct API rejects inputs above its real bound (missing 1M beta header, lower account ITPM, or a 429), the request fails post-flight and the fallback chain (claude-sonnet-5, then claude-headless) takes over, so a ~900k-token prompt can be silently rerouted through the CLI subscription / Bedrock account, outside the metering and budgeting that applied to the original route.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not treat a partial, cross-transport probe as calibration for the API route. Either keep effective_input_ceiling at the previously measured API bound (or leave the entry uncalibrated with conservative_default) until tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --transport api has run on a host with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or, if the 936k bound must ship now, pair it with the required beta_headers entry and a verified account_limits.itpm. Consider having cheval refuse to treat an entry as calibrated when probe_outcome is partial or when ceiling_calibration.transport does not match the entry's own auth_type/transport, and add a per-call cost ceiling check so a loosened token gate cannot become an unbounded spend path.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/cycle-124-effort-flag.bats: @test "c127-2-1: --model opus with no --effort reports high from the catalog"
findings.cross_file_justification: The new params.default_effort value flows from the catalog (diff) through cheval's resolver (not in diff) into the Anthropic HTTP body output_config.effort and the headless adapter's --effort argv, and into the MODELINV payload whose schema enumerates effort/effort_effective. The tests added in this diff define the coverage for that path.
findings.description: params.default_effort is a new operator-controlled value that reaches the wire. The only rejection coverage added is the JSON-schema bats case (validate_v3 refusing "ultra", "HIGH", etc.), which is a CI-time check on the shipped catalog, not a runtime check on the config cheval actually loads (operator overlays, .loa.config.yaml extensions, migrated configs). None of the new pytest or bats tests asserts that cheval itself refuses a default_effort outside EFFORT_LEVELS at the chokepoint, and the single-source test only pins that cheval._EFFORT_LEVELS is the shared tuple. The analogous beta_headers field is documented as a ConfigError at dispatch; default_effort has no such documented or tested guard.
findings.failure_mode: A typo or overlay value such as "HIGH" or "ultra" is sent as output_config.effort (HTTP 400 from the provider, triggering the fallback chain) or passed as a --effort argv element to the CLI, and the MODELINV event records an effort/effort_effective value that violates its own payload schema, breaking downstream trajectory validation. No injection is possible (argv is a list and the body is JSON-serialised), so impact is reliability and telemetry integrity.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate default_effort against loa_cheval.types.EFFORT_LEVELS in the cheval resolver and raise a ConfigError (matching the beta_headers contract). Add a pytest case that feeds a hounfour with params.default_effort: "ultra" to the resolver and expects the typed config error, and a bats dry-run case asserting a non-zero exit.

findings.description: The new ceilingCalibration provenance fields have no cross-field constraints. probe_outcome: partial is documented as valid only when written as source: operator_set, but the schema accepts partial together with source: empirical_probe (the documented gold standard), so a partial bound can be labelled empirical. method: probed_headless is accepted alongside transport: api, and cli_version / cli_model are accepted on probed_api entries. cli_version and cli_model are free-form strings with no maxLength or pattern and are populated verbatim from claude --version subprocess output by the probe tool.
findings.failure_mode: Provenance that cheval and operators rely on to decide staleness and trust can be internally inconsistent without any validation error, weakening the audit trail that justifies ceiling changes like the one in this diff. Unbounded strings copied from subprocess output land in a config file that other tooling and reports render.
findings.suggested_fix: Use JSON Schema 2020-12 if/then blocks inside ceilingCalibration: probe_outcome: partial requires source: operator_set; method: probed_headless requires transport: claude-headless and vice versa; cli_version / cli_model only allowed when method is probed_headless. Add maxLength (e.g. 64) and a conservative pattern to cli_version and cli_model, and extend the V3-add (c127) bats case with these negative combinations.

findings.description: The autouse _offline fixture injects placeholder credentials (sk-ant-test, sk-test, g-test, bedrock-test) into the environment and then patches only http_post / http_post_stream on the openai, google and bedrock modules plus AnthropicAdapter._complete_nonstreaming. The Anthropic streaming path, any transport the adapters reach through a differently named import, and any SigV4/boto path on the Bedrock adapter remain unpatched; offline behaviour depends on every adapter honouring LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING=1. The suite is parametrised over every (provider, model) in the live catalog, so any missed path is exercised for all of them.
findings.failure_mode: A code path that misses the patch makes real outbound HTTPS calls from CI with placeholder keys. Failures surface as unexpected exceptions rather than silent passes (the _http_body guard already covers the empty-body case), so the risk is CI egress, provider-side auth-failure noise and flakiness rather than a false green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hard network guard to the fixture, e.g. monkeypatch socket.socket or http.client.HTTPSConnection.connect to raise, or run the module under pytest-socket --disable-socket, so any unpatched transport fails fast and locally. Include anth_mod in the http_post patch loop as well.

findings.title: Calibrated near-limit requests fail open when provider token count is unavailable
findings.description: In `gate()`, calibrated entries at or above `CALIBRATED_COUNT_NEAR_BOUND` return `warn` and dispatch when no provider counter produced a `count_tokens` estimate. The code comment acknowledges the local estimator can under-count by up to ~2x, so an attacker who controls prompt size can send inputs that appear below the calibrated bound but exceed the provider-measured limit. In an exposed service this is a practical resource-exhaustion path: repeated oversized requests bypass local preflight and are forwarded until the upstream rejects them, consuming bandwidth, queue slots, and provider/API capacity. The safer behavior for calibrated bounds without authoritative counting is fail-closed or require a stricter local bound.

location.anchor: gate(): `if decision.calibrated and in_count_band and est.method != "count_tokens": ... return _out("warn", ... "dispatching")`

findings.recommendation: Change this branch to `preempt` or apply a conservative local cap such as `est.tokens * 2 <= bound` before dispatch. If dispatch-on-warn is required for operators, gate it behind an explicit unsafe override and add rate limiting for repeated upstream context-limit failures.
findings.failure_mode: In `gate()`, calibrated entries at or above `CALIBRATED_COUNT_NEAR_BOUND` return `warn` and dispatch when no provider counter produced a `count_tokens` estimate.

findings.trigger_anchor: if (not calibrated or foreign) and observed is not None and _pos_int(observed) and observed - 1 < value:
findings.description: The cycle-127 r251-1 change lets the persisted observed provider limit (.run/ceiling-observed.json, path taken from LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH) override a calibrated bound whenever ceiling_calibration.transport is foreign to the HTTP route. The only validation on the observed value is _pos_int, so an observed value of 1 produces value=0 with basis 'observed'; the gate then preempts every request on that route. Before this change calibrated entries ignored observations entirely. The accompanying tests pin claude-opus-5-5 as the live foreign-transport entry, and it is the catalog's `opus` alias target, so the primary production route now inherits exposure to a poisoned, stale, or mis-parsed observation. The observation is written by the self-correction from parsed error text (see CEIL-002), and nothing in the diff bounds it against the entry's context_window or the calibrated value, nor records in the envelope that an observation overrode a calibration.
findings.failure_mode: Availability: a single bad observation (tiny parsed limit, stale transient provider limit, or a crafted observed file) clamps the calibrated claude-opus-5-5 bound to as low as 0, and all dispatches are preempted with 'estimated N input tokens > 0 input bound (observed)' until the observation file is manually cleared.
findings.suggested_fix: Before honoring an observation against a calibrated foreign-transport bound, require it to be plausible: at or above a minimum floor (e.g. a fraction of the calibrated value or a fixed minimum like 1,000 tokens), not above context_window, recent (respect stale_after_days), and attributed to the same model and the HTTP transport. Surface an explicit flag in as_envelope when basis=='observed' overrode calibrated=True so operators can see the override.

findings.description: The new fallback regex is not anchored to the Claude Code pre-flight sentence it is meant to parse ('the request is ~N tokens (limit M) but ...'). Any error text containing 'N tokens (limit M)' matches, including unrelated limits (rate limits, output or tool limits) or text echoed from a prompt or tool result through the headless CLI's stderr. The parsed 'limit' is what the self-correction persists as the observed provider ceiling, which CEIL-001 now applies to the calibrated production route. Whether a _CONTEXT_LIMIT_MARKERS check gates this match could not be confirmed from the diff; the function body shown falls through to this pattern after the two stricter ones fail.
findings.failure_mode: A spurious or attacker-influenced 'N tokens (limit M)' string is recorded as a genuine context-limit observation, lowering the route's input bound and feeding the preempt-everything condition in CEIL-001.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the pattern to the CLI's phrasing (require the 'the request is' prefix or equivalent), accept the match only when the message also contains a context-limit marker, and reject parsed limits below a plausible floor or above the entry's context_window before they are persisted.

findings.description: The committed probe report embeds the operator's local account name and home directory in `cli_bin` and `argv[0]`, plus the exact cloud route in `host_route`, `cli_model`, and `route_env` (Bedrock, us-east-1, global prefix, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK). No credentials are present, but this is a durable repository artifact that fingerprints the operator workstation and the production inference route.
findings.failure_mode: Anyone with read access to the repo learns a valid local username, the ~/.local/bin wrapper path, and the Bedrock region/route in use. That supports targeted phishing of the operator and tells an attacker exactly which wrapper path to plant or replace on the host.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the probe report writer redact `cli_bin`/`argv[0]` to the basename or a `~`-relative path, drop `route_env` or reduce it to an allowlist of non-identifying keys, and keep `host_route` generic. Add a small test that fails if a report under grimoires/loa/reports contains `/home/`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test pins behavior of gate() in loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py (not in the diff): for a calibrated entry with a heuristic estimate at or above 0.5x the bound and no provider count (counter is None or returns None), the action is 'warn' and the request is dispatched rather than preempted.
findings.description: The pre-dispatch gate fails open for calibrated entries. The module docstring states the heuristic under-counts the tokenizer by 1.4-1.8x, and the probe report confirms 1.81x on all three successful samples (696136/385000, 880634/487500, 972887/538750). Any heuristic estimate above roughly 0.55x the bound with no count is therefore very likely over the real bound, yet the gate dispatches it. Anything that makes the counter unavailable (counter not wired, count_tokens outage, rate limit, exception swallowed to None) silently disables the control instead of stopping the request.
findings.failure_mode: Oversize requests are sent to the provider and rejected after the fact. Effects are wasted round trips and latency, possible billing on routes that charge for rejected prompts, noisy warn envelopes, and a counter outage becoming a bypass of the gate. The provider remains the real enforcement point, so impact is availability and cost rather than confidentiality.
findings.suggested_fix: When no count is available for a calibrated entry, scale the heuristic by the calibration's known ratio (measured_input_tokens divided by the probe's estimate, both already recorded) and preempt if the scaled estimate exceeds the bound. Alternatively preempt above a conservative fraction (about 0.55x) and reserve 'warn' for the band below it. Update the test to assert preempt for a 0.6x estimate with no count once the policy changes.

findings.cross_file_justification: parse_context_limit in loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py (not in the diff) produces the `limit` that is persisted to .run/ceiling-observed.json. test_ceiling_calibration_transport.py shows input_bound() trusts that observed value to tighten a foreign-transport calibrated bound to observed-1 whenever it is below the calibration, with no lower plausibility check (observed=500_001 yields bound 500_000; the live-entry test accepts ceiling-100_000+1).
findings.description: The parser is being widened to accept loose shapes from CLI text: 'N tokens (limit M)', 'limit: M', '~' prefixes, and comma-grouped digits. The transport tests confirm any parsed limit below the calibrated bound is accepted as authoritative and only ever tightens. The docstring says observations are restricted to 'the context classes only', but the diff gives no evidence of a plausibility bound on the parsed number or of provenance checks (for example requiring size_origin == 'provider'). The implementation could not be verified because ceiling.py is not in the diff; this finding is based on the behavior the new tests pin.
findings.failure_mode: A single mis-parsed or attacker-influenced message carrying a small limit (for example text containing 'limit 1' that also matches the context-limit phrase) is persisted and clamps the route, after which every request for that model on the HTTP transport is preempted until an operator clears the .run file. Because observations never loosen the bound there is no self-correction. Sources of such text include the local CLI wrapper, a proxy in the path, model output echoed into an error, or a stale or corrupted .run file.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist an observed limit only when is_context_limit_message passes AND the failure is attributed to the provider (size_origin == 'provider' with an api_status present), not to local CLI pre-flight text. Reject parsed limits outside a plausibility window (for example below 0.25x context_window or above context_window) and require input_tokens > limit for internal consistency. Record provenance (message hash, timestamp, transport) alongside the observed value so /loa can explain a tightened bound, and create .run/ceiling-observed.json with owner-only permissions. Add negative tests to test_ceiling_cli_limit_parse.py for implausible limits and non-provider shapes.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test pins the behaviour of tools/ceiling-probe-live.py: when CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is unset the probe resolves `claude` from PATH and the calibration record stores `cli_bin == "claude"` (bare name) rather than the resolved absolute path. The record feeds `--write-catalog` into .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml with `source: operator_set, method: probed_headless`.
findings.description: The calibration record that becomes catalog provenance records the CLI as the bare PATH name `claude`, not the resolved absolute path (and no digest). The first test shows the record does carry a full path when CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is set, so provenance quality depends on how the operator invoked the tool. A catalog entry written from a PATH-shadowed or wrapper `claude` is indistinguishable from one written from the real CLI.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or CI job with a shadowed `claude` earlier on PATH (wrapper script, stale install, planted binary) produces a `clean` record that writes a bogus `effective_input_ceiling` into the shared defaults catalog, and the record offers no way to tell which binary produced it.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the probe resolve the binary with shutil.which() before the --version call, record the absolute path (and optionally a sha256 of the file) in `cli_bin`, and refuse to `--write-catalog` when resolution fails. Update the test to assert the resolved path, e.g. `record["cli_bin"] == str(bindir / "claude")`.

findings.trigger_anchor: env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "PYTHONPATH")}
findings.description: The out-of-process test forwards the developer's entire environment to the child except two deny-listed names. Other credential-bearing variables that the real Claude CLI honours (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_SESSION_TOKEN for Bedrock) still reach the subprocess. Exposure is currently nil because CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is pinned to the recording fake and PATH is emptied, so the deny-list is doing no real work and gives a false sense that credentials were scrubbed.
findings.failure_mode: If a future edit loosens the binary pin (for example to test PATH fallback out-of-process), real provider credentials are already present in the child env and a live `claude -p` with a ~400K-token prompt would run and bill the operator's account without touching the cheval ledger the module guard watches.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the child environment from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG/LC_*, TMPDIR, CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN, FAKE_LOG, FAKE_LIMIT_TOKENS) instead of copying os.environ with a deny-list, so no credential can leak into the subprocess regardless of the developer's shell.

findings.cross_file_justification: The writer under test is write_catalog_operator_set in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py (not in the diff). The diff-touched tests show it splices cli_version (taken from `claude --version` stdout, e.g. "9.9.9 (Fake Claude)"), --host-route and cli_model into both YAML scalar values and a provenance comment line by text editing, and no test exercises values containing newlines, '#', ':' or quotes.
findings.description: write_catalog_operator_set performs a line-oriented text edit of model-config.yaml and inserts externally sourced strings: cli_version comes from the subprocess output of the claude binary resolved via CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN/PATH, host_route and cli_model come from CLI flags. The tests assert these appear verbatim in reprobe_trigger, in ceiling_calibration.cli_version, and in a '# cycle-127 FR-3' comment line, but never test a value containing a newline, '#', ':' or a quote. If the writer does not quote/escape, a crafted `claude --version` output or --host-route value could break out of the scalar and add or alter YAML keys in the routing catalog.
findings.failure_mode: A binary answering `--version` with a multi-line or YAML-metacharacter string (or an operator typo in --host-route) produces a catalog that either fails yaml.safe_load (bricking routing) or silently gains injected keys under the model entry. Practical impact is low because controlling the claude binary already implies code execution as the operator.
findings.suggested_fix: Have write_catalog_operator_set reject or sanitize cli_version/host_route/cli_model (strip control characters, cap length, emit via yaml-safe quoting for scalars and strip newlines/'#' from the comment). Add a test that passes cli_version="1.0\nproviders: {}" and host_route="x # y" and asserts the output still safe_loads to the expected structure with the value quoted.

findings.description: The test reads two PIDs from a pidfile written by a child it does not own, polls /proc/<pid>/stat for up to 10 s, and then sends SIGKILL to any PID that still looks alive. There is no check that the PID still belongs to the wrapper or grandchild (no start-time comparison, no Popen handle). If the tool's process-group kill succeeded and the kernel recycled either PID for an unrelated process of the same user within the wait window, the test would SIGKILL that process.
findings.failure_mode: On a busy CI host with low pid_max or aggressive PID recycling, the cleanup path can kill an unrelated same-user process, corrupting other test jobs or developer sessions. The window is narrow and the blast radius is limited to the invoking user.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify PID identity before killing: compare the process start time from /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 recorded at first observation, or have the wrapper write its own cmdline marker and check /proc/<pid>/cmdline before os.kill. Alternatively use a PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER or a dedicated cgroup/session so the test can enumerate its own descendants rather than trusting raw PIDs.
