findings.description: The headless transport writes operator-supplied (--host-route) and CLI-reported (cli_version) free text into model-config.yaml via textual line edits. Neither the diff nor the tests show quoting/escaping of those values, and no test exercises a host-route or cli_version containing YAML-significant characters.
findings.failure_mode: A host route or CLI version string containing a newline or colon injects additional keys (e.g., an overriding effective_input_ceiling or a different model entry) into the catalog, or produces a file that fails to parse and takes cheval down at load time. Because the write is atomic and the record claims written_ceiling, the corruption is silent until the next consumer reads the catalog.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize every written scalar with yaml.safe_dump(value, default_style='"').strip() or an equivalent quoting routine, reject values containing \n or \r before the first paid call (alongside the existing pre-flight prerequisite checks), and add a test writing a host route like `x: 1\neffective_input_ceiling: 1` that asserts the parsed catalog is unchanged apart from the intended fields.

findings.description: `--write-partial-as-operator-set` writes a budget-capped, unbracketed measurement under `source: operator_set`. The schema test explicitly asserts `probe_outcome` is NOT required, so nothing forces consumers or future writers to carry the provenance distinction. A consumer that branches on `source` alone treats the partial value as an operator-vouched calibration with the operator's stale_after_days window.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream staleness and trust logic keyed on `source == operator_set` accepts a machine-produced partial bound as hand-verified evidence. The written value is a verified lower bound, so the direct risk is mis-attribution rather than an oversize ceiling, but the audit trail no longer distinguishes vouched-from-probe from hand-set.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `probe_outcome` required whenever `method` is `probed_headless` (schema `if/then`), or write such entries under a distinct source such as `operator_set_from_partial_probe`. Add a schema test that a `probed_headless` entry without `probe_outcome` is rejected.

findings.description: The record JSON and stderr carry raw provider error bodies (`detail`, 300 chars), OS error strings with paths (`error`: 'catalog not written ... No space left'), the interrupting exception text (`interrupted`), and for non-^C exceptions a full Python traceback including local function names. Probe records are evidence artifacts that are likely committed alongside the catalog change.
findings.failure_mode: Provider error bodies from Bedrock or the Anthropic API can include account/route identifiers, ARNs, request IDs or quota details; tracebacks reveal local filesystem layout. Committing the record publishes these to anyone with repo access.
findings.suggested_fix: Redact known identifier patterns (ARNs, request IDs, absolute home paths) before storing `detail`/`error`/`interrupted`, keep the full traceback on stderr only (not in the record), and document that records may contain provider diagnostics before being committed.

findings.description: This test invokes the real `main()` with `--transport claude-headless --budget-usd 20 --max-tokens-probe 400000` and no `fake` fixture. It is only safe because the `tool` fixture (not shown in this part of the diff) is expected to point CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN at the non-existent sentinel `loa-probe-no-real-cli`. The test's own assertion depends on that sentinel string appearing in the error.
findings.failure_mode: If the fixture's env setup is reordered, removed, or the tool gains a PATH fallback to `claude`, a routine `pytest` run on a developer host with a working claude-bedrock wrapper spawns real 100K-400K token requests and spends real money up to the $20 cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Set CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to the sentinel explicitly inside this test via monkeypatch.setenv, and have the tool refuse to run the headless transport when CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is unset or not an absolute path (usage error, exit 2) so there is no PATH-lookup fallback.

findings.message: The new CLI transport forwards the entire parent environment to an environment-selected executable. `_run_capped` builds `env = {**os.environ, ...}` and `_cli_bin` allows `CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN` to choose the binary, so a poisoned environment can cause API keys/AWS credentials present in the process environment to be disclosed to an attacker-controlled executable. This is local-environment dependent, so I would not rate it HIGH without evidence this tool runs in CI or with attacker-controlled env, but it is a meaningful secrets-exposure risk for an operator tool.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the CLI path from a trusted allowlist or require an absolute path owned by the user, and pass a minimal environment containing only the variables the adapter actually needs.
findings.description: The new CLI transport forwards the entire parent environment to an environment-selected executable, creating a local secrets-exposure risk when credentials are present in the process environment.
findings.failure_mode: The new CLI transport forwards the entire parent environment to an environment-selected executable, creating a local secrets-exposure risk when credentials are present in the process environment.

findings.description: write_catalog_operator_set rebuilds part of the model-config.yaml catalog by string interpolation. It strictly validates probe_outcome, sample_size and ceiling, and quotes trigger, cli_version and cli_model with json.dumps, but four values are written raw: calibrated_at is placed inside bare double quotes with no escaping, transport is written as an unquoted scalar, and host_route (as `route`) and cli_model are interpolated into the provenance `# cycle-127 FR-3: ...` comment line. A newline, a double quote or a `#` in any of these breaks out of the intended scalar or comment and lets the caller append arbitrary YAML lines inside the model block (for example a new `effective_input_ceiling:` or `source:` line that the hand-rolled line editor will not notice but the YAML loader will honour). These values arrive from CLI flags and, per the docstring's record/partial semantics, from a previously written probe record file, so a tampered record or copy-pasted argument bypasses the function's own validation of the numeric fields.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted calibrated_at / transport / host_route / cli_model value injects extra YAML keys into the routing catalog, overriding ceilings or calibration provenance that the function deliberately validates elsewhere, and the hand-parsed text editor cannot detect the corruption.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate calibrated_at against a strict ISO-8601 regex (or re-serialize via datetime), restrict transport to a known set (e.g. {'claude-headless','api'}) or emit it via json.dumps, and reject or strip any character outside printable ASCII (and specifically `\n`, `\r`, `#`, `"`) from host_route and cli_model before composing the provenance comment. Optionally round-trip the final text through yaml.safe_load and assert the model block still has the expected key set before os.replace.

findings.description: The retry-after hint is extracted from provider/CLI diagnostic text (result, api_status, or stderr) with _RETRY_AFTER and converted with float() with no range check. The text is attacker-adjacent (it echoes whatever the provider or wrapper prints). A very long digit run makes float() return inf, and any large value is passed into the record and, per the module comments, is honoured by the retry loop. The _RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S = 180 cap is declared here but the sleep logic that must apply it lives in main(), which is not in this diff, so the clamp cannot be verified from the change.
findings.failure_mode: A misbehaving or hostile upstream message such as `retry-after: 99999999` or an overlong digit string either stalls the probe far beyond the intended 180 s per step, or produces inf and makes time.sleep raise OverflowError, aborting a multi-dollar probe run after the tokens were already billed.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp at parse time: `base['retry_after_s'] = min(float(hint.group(1)), _RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S)` guarded by math.isfinite, and have the retry loop apply the same cap defensively.

findings.description: The executable to run is taken from the CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN environment variable (falling back to a bare `claude` resolved via PATH) and is executed twice: _cli_version runs `<bin> --version`, and _run_capped runs the full headless command with the complete inherited environment, which in the intended deployment includes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and AWS credentials for the Bedrock route. Nothing checks that the resolved binary is an absolute path or the expected tool. In a CI job or a shell with directory-scoped env injection (direnv, .envrc, repo task runners), setting CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN or prepending PATH redirects the probe, and all its credentials, to an arbitrary program while the record only logs the basename.
findings.failure_mode: An environment-level override causes the probe to hand ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and AWS credentials to an attacker-chosen binary, which can also return fabricated JSON to poison the measured ceiling written into the catalog.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the binary once with shutil.which and record the absolute path in the probe record; optionally require CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to be absolute and warn when it differs from the PATH-resolved `claude`. Pass a minimal env allow-list to the subprocess (ANTHROPIC_*, AWS_*, CLAUDE_CODE_*, PATH, HOME) instead of the full os.environ.

findings.cross_file_justification: _route_env, _cli_command and _cli_bin are defined in hunks of tools/ceiling-probe-live.py that are not shown in this diff; the diff-touched record construction in _main_cli is what serializes their output to disk and stdout.
findings.description: The record built in _main_cli embeds route_env (whatever _route_env() collects from the process environment), the full CLI argv, cli_bin, and raw CLI stderr-derived `detail` strings copied wholesale from `res` into each sample. The record is then written with a plain open(args.output, "w") (default umask, typically 0644) or printed to stdout. If _route_env() returns any routing credential (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL with embedded basic-auth) or _cli_command places a token on the command line, that secret lands in a shareable JSON artifact. The module comments treat these records as reviewed, shared artifacts ("the live record shows $4.99/MTok billed"), so they are likely to be committed or pasted into reviews.
findings.failure_mode: Credentials or sensitive environment details leak through the probe record file, stdout capture, or CI logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Make _route_env() return an explicit allowlist of non-secret keys (e.g. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_REGION, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL host only) and redact any key matching KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD. Never pass credentials on the CLI command line. Create args.output with os.open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600) and cap/strip CLI `detail` strings before they enter the record.

findings.description: _charge and _retry_wait consume numbers parsed from the CLI's JSON output (cli_reported_cost_usd, measured_input_tokens, retry_after_s) with only isinstance checks. json.loads accepts Infinity and NaN. A reported cost of Infinity passes `reported > 0` and `int(reported * 1_000_000)` raises OverflowError, which is not in any except clause inside step(); it falls into the `except BaseException` branch, charges the estimate, marks the sample interrupted, re-raises, and ends the whole bisection with exit 1. NaN compares False and is silently treated as $0. measured_input_tokens is used in `measured * price_in // 1_000_000` with no type check, so a string value raises TypeError on the same path. The CLI relays provider data, so these values are not fully trusted.
findings.failure_mode: One malformed numeric field from the CLI terminates the bisection after money has been spent, or a non-finite cost is silently accounted as $0.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize numeric fields in _classify before they reach _charge/_retry_wait: require int/float, math.isfinite, and 0 <= value <= a sane ceiling; treat anything else as missing so the estimate fallback applies. Add OverflowError/TypeError handling in step() that classifies the attempt as `other` rather than aborting.

findings.cross_file_justification: write_catalog_operator_set, i2_clamped and _write_text_atomic are defined outside the shown hunks; the diff-touched _main_cli passes operator free text and subprocess-derived strings into them and performs the pre-spend dry run.
findings.description: --host-route (documented as free text), --cli-model, and cli_version (stdout of the CLI binary) flow unvalidated into write_catalog_operator_set, which takes catalog text and returns new catalog text, i.e. it edits the catalog at the text level. If it templates values without proper quoting, a value containing a newline or structural characters can inject or overwrite other keys (for example another model's effective_input_ceiling), and the catalog then feeds gen-adapter-maps.sh and the review-skill build. The pre-spend dry run does not exercise the same inputs as the real write: it omits cli_version and force_partial and passes cli_arg where the real write passes _resolved_cli_model(cli_arg). A value that breaks or injects on the real write is therefore only discovered after paid probing, contrary to the stated 'fail before any spend' intent (r251-1 P6).
findings.failure_mode: Catalog corruption or key injection from unvalidated strings; late write failure after spend.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate host_route, cli_model and cli_version in _main_cli against a conservative pattern (single line, printable, length cap). Compute cli_version and _resolved_cli_model before the dry run and pass the dry run exactly the kwargs the final write uses. Ensure write_catalog_operator_set serializes through a parser (yaml/json dump) rather than string templating, and re-parses its output before returning.

findings.description: The --budget-usd cap is enforced only against est_micro, derived from filler tokens times `ratio`, and ratio is None (treated as 1.0) until a step has measured. The code's own comment says the Opus 4.7+ tokenizer counts the filler about 1.8x heavier, so the first step at --max-tokens-probe can be billed roughly 1.8x its estimate and the run can exceed the cap by up to 80% of the largest step. The pre-flight 'worst-case step' and 'N such steps fit' message is understated by the same factor. A size rejection with no parsable count and no CLI-reported cost is charged $0, so spent_usd can also under-report real spend.
findings.failure_mode: Actual provider spend exceeds the operator's cap and the recorded spent_usd under-reports it.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply a conservative initial ratio (e.g. 2.0) to the first step's estimate and to the worst-case line until a measurement exists, or multiply est_micro by a safety factor in the pre-check. State the possible overshoot explicitly in the pre-flight message.

findings.trigger_anchor: docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md: 'The agy (Antigravity) route is opt-in, default off.'
findings.description: The migration guide documents that the agy (`gemini-headless`) adapter still places the full redacted review diff on the CLI's argv, readable by every local account through /proc/<pid>/cmdline and ps. The same exposure is documented for gemini when an operator passes --sandbox in gemini_extra_flags. The change gates the route behind `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` rather than removing the exposure, and tells operators to enable it 'knowing the argv exposure'. This is an accepted-risk disclosure path for review content (which may contain secrets, pre-disclosure vulnerability fixes, or proprietary code) on any multi-user reviewer host.
findings.failure_mode: On a shared host with agy_opt_in enabled, any unprivileged local account can read the entire review diff from the agy process's command line for the duration of the hop.
findings.suggested_fix: Deliver the prompt to agy through a file inside the adapter's private 0700 workspace (as the grok adapter already does) or via stdin, and fall back to argv only if agy offers no other input. If argv remains the only option, refuse the route when /proc is not mounted with hidepid and other sessions are present, and document that condition rather than relying on operator judgement.

findings.trigger_anchor: docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md: 'The key is read from `.loa.config.yaml` alone (a framework defaults file cannot opt you in)'
findings.cross_file_justification: The CHANGELOG hunk in this diff explains that every headless adapter was moved to an isolated cwd precisely because 'the caller's directory is the tree under review, whose CLAUDE.md ... would otherwise shape its own reviewer'. The new agy_opt_in key is read from `.loa.config.yaml`, a project-tree file, and `companion_chain`/`flatline_protocol` blocks live in the same file. If the dissent loads that file from the checkout being reviewed rather than from a trusted base ref, the reviewed change can reconfigure its own reviewer (route selection, companion opt-out, agy opt-in). Needs verification against the loader in cheval and adversarial-review.sh, which are not in this diff.
findings.description: The opt-in that re-enables the argv-exposing agy route, and the companion_voice / companion_chain controls that decide how many independent voices review a change, are all read from `.loa.config.yaml` inside the project tree. The diff's own rationale for cwd isolation (the reviewed tree must not shape its reviewer) is not applied to this configuration source. A pull request can edit `.loa.config.yaml` in the same change it wants reviewed.
findings.failure_mode: A change under review sets `flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice: false` (dropping the second voice without DEGRADED status) or flips `agy_opt_in: true` so the reviewer pushes the diff to the argv-exposing adapter; the review of that change runs under the attacker-chosen configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Read dissent-governing configuration (companion_voice, companion_chain, agy_opt_in, repair model) from the base ref or from a location outside the reviewed tree, or treat any `.loa.config.yaml` change in the reviewed diff as a mandatory INCONSISTENT/DEGRADED trigger so a reviewer sees that the reviewer's own settings were altered by the change.
